action: A long-necked bird standing facing left squashes into a tangled vertical bundle and re-emerges facing right, lowering its head as if pecking or drinking.
identity_gap: The doodle's long, low horizontal body with a row of separate leg strokes is compressed into a tall, narrow cluster; during the turn (and after it) the legs and back become a tangle of crossing lines, so the body plan no longer matches.
notes: Frames 1-3 keep the doodle's head (almond eye, snout tick) and flat back stroke and are recognizably the same drawing, though squashed vertically. Frames 4-5 lose the figure entirely as a scribble rather than reading as a turn, and frames 6-8 come back mirrored and heavier, read better as a hunched bird than as the doodle's long-necked four-legged animal.
